subject: MicroFoundry — follow-up: microbatching econ options & next steps

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: MicroFoundry — follow-up: microbatching econ options & next steps

Hi Samir / Elaine,

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciated the practical walkthrough of your inference flow and how you shard requests into tiny batches. A quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Key signals from our side: your trial trace shows short requests (~40–80 tokens avg) with high QPS spikes. That pattern is a great fit for microbatching + prefix caching, which typically improves $/1M-token economics by 15–30% for workloads like yours.
- Immediate ask from you: confirm a target blended unit price (e.g., $/1M tokens) or a monthly budget range so we can map pricing bands and a committed-use proposal. You mentioned a runway target — can you confirm a rough monthly spend band (e.g., <$25k / $25–75k / >$75k)?
- Optional: if MicroFoundry’s founders are open to a short pilot commitment, we can include a Founder Discount for the first 3–6 months. To make that concrete I’ll need a short usage snapshot and target discount ask (percent or target $/1M).

Attached: I’ve included a small template you can fill (microfoundry_usage_snapshot.csv) and our quick pricing primer (redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf) to show baseline unit economics across model sizes and quantization.

Next steps: if you can reply with the snapshot and a budget range by Thu EOD PST, I’ll run three scenarios and get Ben to attach committed-use and 2/3-year incentive examples.

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers.

—Vanessa

Vanessa,

Thanks for the recap — helpful. Quick answers:
- Budget band: we’re planning for roughly $40k–$60k/month initially (scaling after Q4 depending on uptake).
- Target unit price: we don’t have a firm $/1M number in mind; the team asked if you can show a target range and what a Founder Discount would look like (we’d like to see a 20–30% sweetener in the first 3–6 months if possible).

I attached a brief usage export from our test harness in the call (see microfoundry_usage_snapshot.csv). It’s noisy but should be enough to model. Also, two quick questions:
1) If we commit to a 12-month reserved profile, what’s the break-even vs pay-as-you-go?
2) For multi-year incentives, how flexible are ramp/step-up schedules?

Elaine (cc) will review the econ with me. Looking forward to the scenarios.

—Samir

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <sam@microfoundry.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MicroFoundry — follow-up: microbatching econ options & next steps

Hi Samir / Elaine — appreciate the snapshot. I ran three scenario sketches (high-level, ballpark):

Scenario A — Pay-as-you-go (no commitment):
- Baseline blended unit: $18 / 1M tokens (current recommended model mix with microbatching savings applied)
- Effective range with microbatching optimizations: $14–18 / 1M tokens depending on spike smoothing

Scenario B — 12‑month committed use (monthly commit = $45k):
- Discount band applied: 18% off baseline => ~$14.8 / 1M tokens
- 12-month payment terms with quarterly reconciliation; break-even vs PAYG about 8–10 months given current load profile

Scenario C — Multi-year (24–36 month) with ramp & milestone rebate:
- Year 1: 15% off baseline, Year 2: 20% off baseline (could be structured as volume thresholds or a stepped rebate)
- If you guarantee a minimum monthly commit + growth milestones, we can reach $11–13 / 1M tokens by year 3 in the model we ran (includes reserved slot scheduling and deeper quantization on lower-sensitivity models)

Founder Discount (ad hoc): if Leadership approves, a one-time Founder Sponsor credit (applied as invoices/credits) of 20% for months 1–3 is possible — this is discretionary and needs an approval note from Marissa / Partner Ops. I’ve attached a quick pricing sheet to show the math.

Open items:
- Precise token distribution (in the CSV we got, average token size and peak percentiles would refine these numbers)
- Desired commitment cadence (monthly vs quarterly billing)

I’ll stand by to formalize into a proposal once we lock the commit level you want.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0213

Attachment stub: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (pricing workbook, model/quantization assumptions)
